correctness.rationale: For commuting idempotents e and f the product p=ef=fe has im(p)=im(e)∩im(f), which is fixed pointwise by both. Its fibers canonically partition into the root b, e-only fixed points A, f-only fixed points C, and free points D. The two maps on D may target respectively {b}∪A and {b}∪C independently, giving ((a+1)(c+1))^d arrangements. Labeled exponential assembly proves the complete EGF and image-rank support constraints. Independent direct map-composition enumeration matches every coefficient through n=6 and exact support through n=8; finite computations corroborate, not prove, the general theorem.

value.rationale: The three-variable EGF determines a full natural invariant of commuting idempotent pairs (the two individual image sizes and the product image size), not available from the classical one-idempotent rank table. The canonical product-fiber classification gives all coefficients for arbitrary n and sharp necessary-and-sufficient support inequalities, including a constructive realization for each feasible rank triple. It offers a reusable structural tool for statistics of simultaneous retractions and nontrivial commuting correlation; the complete classification is substantive rather than an arbitrary slice.
